identity.title: Statistical Test for Feature Selection Pipelines by Selective Inference

problem.claim: Assess the statistical significance of data-analysis pipelines, particularly feature-selection pipelines.

contributions.claim: A selective-inference framework for constructing statistical tests applicable to feature-selection pipelines built from predefined components.
A theoretical guarantee for controlling false-positive feature selection probability at any desired level.
A framework for testing any configuration of the specified feature-selection pipelines without extra implementation costs.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe their statistical test as novel and distinguish the framework by supporting arbitrary predefined-component feature-selection pipelines.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report a proof that the test controls false-positive feature selection probability at any desired level.
The authors report demonstrating validity and effectiveness on synthetic and real data.
As a proof of concept, the framework covers linear-model pipelines combining three imputation, three outlier-detection, and three feature-selection algorithms.

narrative_sequence.summary: Defines data-analysis pipelines as structured sequences integrating analysis algorithms to transform raw data into insights.
Introduces a statistical test for assessing pipeline significance, based on selective inference.
Claims systematic applicability to feature-selection pipelines composed of predefined components and instantiates this for linear models with three algorithm choices in each of three stages.
Reports false-positive control at any desired level and experiments on synthetic and real data.
Presents an implementation framework intended to test every pipeline configuration without additional implementation cost.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a broad applicability claim with a concrete proof-of-concept pipeline space and a stated statistical error-control guarantee.

lessons.interpretation: A claim becomes easier to assess when its scope and decisive guarantee are stated alongside a concrete instantiation.
lessons.application: State the supported component space, instantiate it with explicit algorithm counts or categories, and name the controlled error quantity and target level.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when component choices or the relevant error criterion cannot be specified in advance.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the test statistic, selective-inference construction, or how arbitrary component configurations are represented.
Experimental sample sizes, baselines, metrics, and numerical results are not reported.
The meaning of “without extra implementation costs” and the conditions underlying the theoretical guarantee are unspecified.
